Create an mvgam formula object

Source: R/priors.R
mvgam_formula.Rd

Constructs a lightweight mvgam formula object that combines observation and trend model formulas. The inspection functions get_prior(), stancode() and standata() take it.

Usage

mvgam_formula(formula, trend_formula = NULL)

Arguments

formula

An object of class formula, brmsformula, or mvbrmsformula describing the observation model.

trend_formula

An optional formula describing trend dynamics. Default NULL results in pure brms equivalent model. See Details for trend syntax.

Value

An object of class c("mvgam_formula", base_class) where base_class is the class of the input formula, containing:

  • formula: The observation model formula

  • trend_formula: The trend model formula (or NULL)

Details

The mvgam_formula object is a minimal container that pairs an observation formula with an optional trend formula. Data, family, and other model specifications are provided when calling inspection or fitting functions:

get_prior(mvgam_formula(y ~ x, ~ AR()), data = dat, family = poisson())

When trend_formula = NULL, the model reduces to a pure brms observation model. When specified, the trend_formula can include:

  • Trend constructors: RW(), AR(), CAR(), ZMVN(), VAR(), LLT(), PW()

  • Covariates that affect trend dynamics

  • Smooth terms using mgcv syntax: s(), t2()

  • Random effects: (1|group), (slope|group)

  • Gaussian processes: gp()

Trend formula restrictions

The trend_formula has specific restrictions to maintain compatibility with State-Space dynamics and prevent conflicts between observation-level and trend-level modeling:

Forbidden Terms:

  • brms addition-terms: weights(), se(), cens(), trunc(), trials(), rate(), vreal(), vint(), subset(), index(), dec(), cat(), thres()

  • Missing-value imputation: mi()

  • brms autocorrelation: ar(), ma(), arma(), cosy(), unstr(), autocor()

  • Offset terms: offset()

Rationale: Addition terms change the observation model, through weights, censoring or exposure. They belong in the observation formula. Autocorrelation terms conflict with the trend's state-space dynamics. brms imputes a mi() predictor as a response of the model. A trend formula holds no response.

Multivariate models, single shared trend type

For multivariate observation models (mvbind() or bf() + bf()), a single trend constructor applies to all responses. Different trend types per response (e.g. RW() for one response and AR(p = 3) for another) are not supported and will not be added. mvgam stores latent trend states in a single lv_trend matrix with shared dynamics parameters; mixing trend types per response would require parallel dynamics machinery throughout the codegen, sampling, and prediction pipelines.

What multivariate models support:

  • Different observation families per response (e.g. bf(count ~ x, family = poisson()) + bf(biomass ~ x, family = Gamma())).

  • Different fixed-effect, smooth, or GP terms per response in the observation formulas.

  • Hierarchical / grouped trends via the gr argument on the (single) trend constructor.

If you need different dynamics per response, fit independent univariate mvgam() models for each response.

Examples:


# Correct usage
mvgam_formula(y ~ x + weights(w), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1))
mvgam_formula(count ~ offset(log_exposure), trend_formula = ~ RW())

# Incorrect usage (will error)
mvgam_formula(y ~ x, trend_formula = ~ AR() + weights(w))
mvgam_formula(y ~ x, trend_formula = ~ RW() + offset(z))
